description: Gym Electric Motor is a Python simulation package from the Paderborn University LEA developers for testing electric-drive controllers. It provides Gymnasium environments combining an electrical supply, power converter, motor and mechanical load. Supported drive families include DC, synchronous and induction machines. Users select a physical system and reference trajectories, then supply continuous duty cycles or discrete switching actions through a controller. The environments return simulated observations and rewards for control experiments. Spatial coverage is the configured drive, while time steps and episode lengths are user-defined. Source, documentation and examples are openly available through GitHub and the Python package under MIT, free of charge. Reuse includes reinforcement-learning experiments and comparisons with conventional drive control for industrial machinery or electrified transport. A limitation is that simulated motor and load parameters need to represent the intended equipment; success in an environment alone does not establish hardware performance. No directly related existing catalogue record was established. This review did not run a controller or connect equipment.
